scientific_conclusion: The accumulated reduced-state drift is not supported as a generic self-amplifying manifold instability under the frozen C2 rules.
Occasional local tangent gains above one exist, especially at the initial 5-cm RISE/CYCLE states, but they are too sparse to explain the persistent multi-interval drift.
Repeated local teacher-reference closure bias is therefore the supported mechanism class across all eight width/history cases.
A global stabilizer, projection-to-manifold correction or new memory state is not justified by C2.
C1R remains mechanistically relevant: state-shape drift is robustly state-drift-dominant after accumulation, while local qi and qH closure errors are important in the difficult thin-terminal cases.

next_research_authority.question: Which signed local closure-bias channels inject the persistent mass-neutral state-shape error, under which H-motion regimes, and with what conservation-consistent contribution?
